concerns.text: SC-002 states: 'The extrapolation R² score on the novel set is measured against the expected degradation target of < 0.50'. This is an unmeasurable success criterion because the 'novel' set is defined as compositions with no ground-truth DFT data. Without ground truth, R² cannot be calculated. The spec acknowledges this in US-3 ('if ground-truth DFT data is unavailable... analyze prediction uncertainty'), but SC-002 mandates a specific R² threshold that is impossible to verify if the primary assumption (availability of ground truth for the novel set) fails. A success criterion must be verifiable under the defined conditions.

SC-005 states: 'The reliability metric validity is measured by the ability to rank the top 100 novel candidates by uncertainty, where the top candidates must exhibit ensemble variance within the lower tail of the predicted distribution'. This is circular and unmeasurable. 'Lower tail' is a relative statistical property of the distribution itself, not an absolute threshold. Any set of 100 candidates ranked by lowest variance will inherently be in the 'lower tail' of that specific distribution. There is no external reference or absolute value to verify against, making it impossible to determine if the criterion is met or failed.

US-3 Independent Test states: '...comparing the model's R² on the novel set against the training set (expecting a drop to < 0.50)'. Similar to SC-002, this test is unverifiable if the 'novel' set lacks ground truth. The spec defines 'novel' as compositions absent from training data and APIs. If no DFT data exists for these, R² is undefined. The test procedure must be conditional: 'If ground truth exists, calculate R²; else, verify uncertainty correlation with distance from convex hull.' As written, the test is impossible to execute for the primary use case (novel compositions).
